title: Illustration / Characters / Posing
slide_intent: Choose poses that convey personality while preserving a readable silhouette so expression does not collapse into visual confusion.
strategic_value: Active human poses and a character-specific exception can help Duolingo make its cast feel alive without applying one pose rule mechanically.
demonstration: Three rows compare expressive poses with rejected alternatives; the final row uses a gorilla to show the need to keep large color blocks distinct.
practical_value: Try expressive poses, then adjust the choice to the character’s proportions and the separation of its major color areas.

content_islands.name: Human-pose comparisons
content_islands.spec: Place two human-character rows at upper left, showing expressive alternatives before a crossed static pose in each row.

content_islands.name: Gorilla exception
content_islands.spec: Place the gorilla comparisons below, retaining the rejected blocky pose beside alternatives that separate the large forms.

content_islands.name: Pose rationale and exception
content_islands.spec: Place Posing and two paragraphs at right, explaining both the general preference for expression and the gorilla-specific static-pose guidance.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text links posing with personality and storytelling and warns that static, expressionless characters can feel lifeless.
reference_purposes.Application: The comparisons test poses against different character structures.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The general preference against static poses is qualified: the gorilla’s large color blocks are best kept separated in a static pose.

ingredient.name: Character-specific posing
ingredient.role: Show personality while keeping the character readable.
ingredient.application: Prefer expressive poses where possible, but test them against the character’s construction; use a separated static pose for the illustrated gorilla case.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. The source’s static-pose exception prevents treating activity as a universal requirement.
